nodes.title: ENTER - Corridor
nodes.text:
You make your way carefully into the dungeon corridor. Damp glistens on the walls, and the air is thick with dust. Feeling your way forward, your eyes slowly begin to adjust to the darkness.

“What have I forgotten to pack?” you ask yourself.

Oh well. Too late now.

You continue for perhaps half a mile without a single junction. The corridor gradually widens, opening into cavernous spaces in places, and you begin to realise that you are slowly but surely descending deeper underground.

You stop to rest.

The darkness around you has become thick and oppressive. You pull out a small flint lantern and strike it. A tiny flame catches on the oil-soaked mantle, casting a weak pool of light around you. You must thank that halfling you met in the Wasted Wizard; if you ever see him again, he parted with this lantern for a hot meal.

It isn’t much, but it is enough to see the tips of your boots and a short distance ahead.

You continue and begin to feel tired; the air is becoming shallow and hard to breath, suddley the corridr open into a junction; some cooler air blows over you like a breath, as though the dungeon itself is breathing! You stop and try not to worry.

As you take your next step, you hear a rumble; out of instinct, you throw yourself on the ground just in time to feel the ground shake and pieces of rock cover you from behind... 

MAKE A DEX ROLL

Lights out!

nodes.title: Door - Make a SNEAK roll
nodes.text:
You listen at the door and hear voices behind. Sounds like some goblins eating and arguing over their food!

"Give me that bone! You had your share! says one. "Get your own, you greedy oaf", cries another.

You can't quite make out how many there are yet, but you figure if you let them argue it out, maybe there'll be one or two less to fight if they keep this up.

nodes.title: Go up stairs
nodes.text:
You climb for a long time up stone-carved steps; maybe this was a real structure back in the dark, as the steps are solid and well-made, and cold air rises from the darkness below.

You reach the top, where it is very dark and plateaus out east and west, it's dark you worry in case there are drops around you.

nodes.title: Store Room
nodes.text: Only accessible if you have the Iron Key.

nodes.title: Troll Bridge
nodes.text:
It's hard to see into the darkness, but just ahead you see what looks like  a deep ravine and a bridge; heading over to the darkness.

You strike up your flint lantern again aware that this will soon run out if you donlt find some oil soon, as you do the cavern widens in your view casting deep shadows deep shadows but you can clearly see a route across the bridge.

The bridge has old wooden wooden planks.

You may roll on your Intelligence.

if you make that roll, go to 327
Begin to walk across the bridge 180
Go back down the stairs to the Junction 100

nodes.title: Troll Den
nodes.text:
You hop, skip and jump across the bridge trap and make it safely to the other side.
Before you is an entrance to a cave.

You peer into the dark cave and walk slowly in (something smells foul for sure); the cave slowly becomes wide and forks off into 2 directions. Bones litter the floor, and there is the smell of something boiling down the right tunnel.

nodes.title: Introduction
nodes.text:
The Ghost Bell

For as long as anyone can remember, the bells of Dragon Reach have watched over the people of the land.

They are not simply rung on holy days, feast days and celebrations. They are also a warning system. If invasion, fire or some other great danger threatens the realm, the bells carry the message from town to town across Dragon Reach.

There are said to be more than three hundred of them, scattered throughout the land, and each community guards its bell carefully. Every town and city appoints a trusted bell warden to look after theirs, keeping it maintained, watching for damage and making sure it is ready to sound when needed.

To be chosen as a bell warden is considered a great honour, and the role is usually given to someone older, dependable and respected.

Tarak the healer is one of those wardens, and he is proud to be so.

On this particular morning, however, Tarak wakes with an uneasy feeling in his bones.

Something is wrong.

He cannot explain it, but he feels restless and on edge.

Still, Tarak is a creature of habit, and so he gets up and begins his usual duties.

He lives near the City of Sisters, in the north-eastern reaches of Dragon Reach, where he serves as one of the local healers. Most of his work is with the nearby villages and settlements, although from time to time he is summoned into the city itself to attend to the emissaries and officials who govern there.

When he is not healing the sick, Tarak has another responsibility.

His bell.

It stands in an old tower south-east of Doomsbury Hollow, close to the ancient mage towers. Tarak visits it regularly, checking the mechanisms, making repairs where needed and keeping the great bell oiled and in working order.

But first, there is today's work.

It is a cool spring morning, and Tarak begins packing his bags and satchels with herbs, bottles and remedies for his rounds. His first stop will be the town square, where people are often already waiting for him by the time he arrives.

Before leaving, though, he needs to prepare his medicines.

At the back of his small but comfortable house on the riverbank is a room hidden behind a false bookcase.

Tarak pulls one particular book.

Click.

The bookcase swings open.

Behind it lies his workshop.

He always feels a small rush of satisfaction when he enters. This is his place. Somewhere he feels completely at home, and somewhere he has spent far too many hours experimenting with herbs, powders, potions and cures.

The shelves are packed from floor to ceiling.

Bottles. Boxes. Leather pouches. Crucibles. Jars of powders. Dried roots. Bundles of herbs. Strange liquids in stranger containers.

To anyone else, the room would probably look hopelessly disorganised.

Tarak knows exactly where everything is.

Some of the contents would appear completely useless to a visitor, which is exactly how Tarak likes it.

Nothing is labelled.

There are no helpful notes explaining what each powder or liquid does.

Unlike those wizards up at the mage towers, healers do not write everything down in enormous books.

Probably because the wizards would forget half their spells after three nights on the ale.

A sensible healer would never prepare a powerful potion, label it clearly and leave it sitting on a shelf for anyone to steal.

Especially now.

There has been too much talk in the taverns of Dargonmarch. Rumours of strangers. Scouts. The Shadow Army.

If an enemy ever got into Tarak's workshop and found shelves filled with clearly labelled potions, the consequences could be disastrous.

No. A good healer makes what he needs when he needs it.

The recipes remain in his head.

And, one day, they will die with him.

This morning, however, Tarak has a problem.

He has run out of Travelling Star.

It is a rare herb and an important ingredient in one of his cures for poison.

Normally that would be inconvenient.

Today it is worrying.

Over the past few days, several locals have become seriously ill after drinking water from nearby wells. Tarak has heard stories of unfamiliar figures seen around the taverns and roads, and he cannot shake the suspicion that the sickness may not be accidental.

He prepares what medicines he can and goes about his rounds.

Later, Tarak makes his regular journey to inspect the bell tower.

That is when everything changes.

The great bell has been shattered.

Not cracked.

Not damaged by age.

Shattered.

The metal itself appears to have been broken apart by a powerful spell.

Worse still, three large pieces of the bell are missing.

Without them, the bell cannot be repaired. And without the bell, this remote corner of Dragon Reach has no way to sound the warning if an attack comes from the north-east.

Tarak stares at the ruined bell.

The uneasiness he felt that morning suddenly makes sense.

Someone has deliberately silenced it.

And if the Shadow Army really is coming, they may already be much closer than anyone realises.

The nearby towns must be warned.

But first, the bell must be restored.

Tarak kneels beside the shattered metal and prepares a tracing potion. He sprinkles the mixture carefully around the base of the tower.

For a few moments, nothing happens.

Then faint footprints begin to glow across the ground.

Someone has been here.

The trail leads away from the bell tower, across the hillside and towards a rocky outcrop nearby.

But first, Tarak needs provisions for the journey.

He hurries back to his house and quickly packs a small backpack. Into it goes the dagger Rill — his closest friend and a younger healer — gave him, along with his flint, oil lantern and a few other light provisions.

It isn’t much, but Tarak has no idea how long he may be gone.

He makes his way back to the bell tower.

The tracing spell is already beginning to fade, the glowing footprints growing fainter with every passing moment.

Tarak studies the last clear marks and sets off in the direction they lead.

Across the hillside.

Towards the rocks.

And whatever is waiting beyond them.

Tarak follows it.

There, hidden among the stones and brambles, he discovers the entrance to an old dungeon.

The footprints disappear into the darkness.

Somewhere below, the thief has taken the three missing pieces of the Ghost Bell.

And perhaps more importantly, Tarak may also find evidence of whoever is poisoning the wells.

He tightens his pack, checks his lantern and steps into the tunnel.

He must recover the three pieces of the bell.

He must find the source of the poison.

And he must do both before the people of Dragon Reach become too weak to fight — or the Shadow Army arrives.

nodes.title: Troll rubbish shoot
nodes.text: You rummage through the piles of stinking bones and discarded previous adventures, only to find a chain mechanism. Will you pull the chain or back away?

nodes.title: Door - Open without listening
nodes.text:
You burst open the door and can see what looks like a small kitchen or eating area to find 2 large goblins staring back at you.

Roll your dexterity or above to quickly slam the door and block it with a nearby latch. This is a heavy, strong door and as long as you hold that latch down, they won't get out.

If you make your DEX roll go to 79

If not go to 246

nodes.title: Goblins - Dead - Kitchen
nodes.text:
Now all the goblins lay slain you look around. This is dirty place that would never get any reviews on Doogle (the wasted wizard notice board). There grease covered burnt pots stacked high, bones and old meat strewn across the floor and the large round table in the middle of the room seems to have a sricky sunstance.

...

nodes.title: Junction: DOOR and STAIRS
nodes.text:
If you did not make the DEX roll you took some hits from the falling rocks, lose 2 health

If you did make the DEX roll, you are ok but a little stunned; either way, continue reading

It's a while before you come round, but when you do, you notice a rockfall now blocks the way back. You feel this is now a one-way trip and take stock; no harm done as such, but you sit for a while and rest. You eventually get to your feet, take a short drink from your water flask and hope you can find more later, and you walk a little further to a junction.

To the right are some steps, hewn out of the rock, but clearly an ascending route to a higher ledge.

To your left is a door set back some 20 feet in the rocks.

nodes.title: Door - Wait
nodes.text:
You are in no rush; these greedy goblins will be asleep after that meal. You wait and take a little time to meditate a little way back in the darkness, just in case they come out and some time passes.

Finally, you quietly approach the door again; you hear the voices and arguing have died down. You wait a little longer and listen, and you hear snoring.

Slowly open the door, and go in, being very careful not to make any sound...

Inside is a 2 goblins, one asleep on the table and the other lying on a straw bed with an empty bottle of what looks like oil next to him. You draw your dagger and expel the nearest one without a sound. It slumps to the floor, and you catch its fall as black blood runs over your hands.

You then approach, and as you do, kick over a can of some kind of slop; roll over your dexterity or higher to stop the pot spinning!

If you do...
you also sneak up and cut the throat of this vile creature before 

it can even see you.

If not, it leaps to its feet, and you must fight it.

The goblin stats: 1 die (no sword ready), 3 HP

You roll one die plus +2 for your basic dagger.

Roll and apply damage for the higher to the other; continue until either is dead.

nodes.title: Bent Lock - Closes kitchen
nodes.text:
You pick up a nearby heavy rock and smash it over the latch repeatedly, bending it so it could never be opened from the inside. You hear the goblins (now realising) pulling and pushing the door to no avail; these dungeon doors are strongly made, and that's stuck fast.

You won't know how that might of turned out but you feel this could have been a nasty encounter.

You head up the stairs, this being the only way left to go.

Go to 27

nodes.title: Goblins dex roll made 1 goblin to fight
nodes.text:
You shove the door with all your might, and a loud clatter of pots and pans, grunts, and groans follows, ending in a loud, bubbling scream! 

As you enter the room, one goblin is scrambling to get up, and the other has fallen headfirst into a massive pot of boiling gruel.

There is now only one goblin; the other is boiled to perfection, and all you see is his feet sticking out of a steaming pot! Ooh, goblin stew!

Fight one goblin... strength 4 + 1 for his sword

Roll one die for you and one for him; add any weapon bonuses. If you score higher, he takes the damage.

e.g. If you roll a 5 plus 2 for a sword, that's 7; if he rolls a 3 plus 1 for his sword, that's 4. You do him 3 hits; he only has 3 HP, so he dies. Repeat the roll until either are dead.

If you win go to 

If you lose go to 52

nodes.title: YOU DIE
nodes.text:
You die! You're dead, out like a candle! Everybody's dead, Dave!

THE END.

Start a new game and be careful this time!
